controls.reason: A workload policy can define the five exact resource request, limit, priority, disruption and eviction behavior fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A workload class missing an eviction rule or resource limit fails the finite policy schema.

controls.reason: Workload-identity records cannot prove shared node or cluster credentials are absent from every workload, bootstrap and emergency path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known workloads can use unique identities while a legacy job inherits the node credential.

controls.reason: Absence of secrets from all image layers, build outputs, process environments and ordinary diagnostic output is an open-world negative claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured scanners can pass while an encoded key remains in an image layer or exception dump.

controls.reason: Restricting all communication to declared flows requires a complete flow inventory and enforcement across every protocol, sidecar, host and control-plane path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Network policies can match declared flows while DNS tunneling or a host-network workload reaches an undeclared destination.

controls.reason: A workload lifecycle policy can define five exact readiness, liveness, startup, graceful-termination and drain behaviors.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting drain or startup behavior fails the finite schema; runtime correctness is not inferred.

controls.reason: Six test executions do not prove complete versions, workloads, topology combinations, data states and recovery oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each named failure can pass alone while node loss during rolling update corrupts storage.

controls.reason: Support and patch status across six component classes requires complete cluster inventory plus changing vendor and vulnerability authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known components can be current while an unmanaged add-on or node image is unsupported.

controls.reason: Preventing untrusted workloads from reaching four sensitive targets is a security property over arbitrary workloads and escape paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known attack tests can fail closed while a host socket mount or metadata proxy exposes another route.

controls.reason: Auditing five privileged action families requires complete API, runtime, node and control-plane path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Registered operations can log while an alternate exec or secret-read interface leaves no audit event.

controls.reason: Autoscaling bounds are inspectable, but preventing scale storms against every dependency is an open workload and runtime interaction claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A maximum replica count can pass while retries cause many functions or clusters to overwhelm one downstream service.

controls.reason: Detection of all configuration drift and unmanaged workloads depends on a complete desired-state and runtime discovery boundary.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The scanner can report no drift while a shadow namespace or out-of-band cluster is never observed.

controls.reason: A rebuild practice record does not prove recovery is complete or that every source, image and dependency is actually trusted.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cluster can rebuild in staging while using a compromised registry mirror or omitting production state.

controls.reason: An inventory cannot prove inclusion of every serverless function, trigger, source, destination, identity, secret, region and failure target.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All rows can be complete while an out-of-band trigger or dynamically created function remains unknown.

controls.reason: An event-source policy can require retry-and-duplicate semantics by default and permit an exception only with a bound authoritative delivery guarantee.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A source marked exactly-once without a valid guarantee reference fails the finite default-and-exception rule.

controls.reason: Handler idempotence and concurrent safety are behavioral properties over every state, side effect, timing and retry interleaving.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known duplicate tests can pass while a timeout after commit creates a second effect on retry.

controls.reason: A serverless policy can define the six exact timeout, memory, payload, temporary-storage, connection and concurrency limits.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A function class missing a connection or payload limit fails the finite configuration schema.

controls.reason: Protecting every downstream dependency from burst scaling and retry amplification requires complete dependency inventory and unbounded workload behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Load tests can pass while an event storm triggers retries that exhaust an indirect provider quota.

controls.reason: Each event workflow can be checked for configured dead-letter, failure destination, replay and reconciliation mechanisms.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting replay or reconciliation from a workflow fails the finite four-mechanism configuration schema.

controls.reason: Controlling public invocation, cross-account triggers and event permissions requires complete functions, accounts, identities and trigger-path inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known policies can pass while an external account retains invocation permission through an inherited resource rule.

controls.reason: Cold-start and scaling measurements depend on workload, region, platform state and user-objective interpretation not defined by the rule.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A small warm-biased test can meet the objective while real cold bursts violate it for users.

controls.reason: Guaranteeing process reuse never leaks state between any users or tenants is a security property over arbitrary invocation sequences and runtimes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Pairwise tests can pass while a rare warm-instance error exposes a prior tenant's cached data.

controls.reason: Propagation of five context fields across every synchronous, asynchronous, retry and provider boundary requires complete path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Standard invocations can pass while a dead-letter replay loses tenant or deadline context.

controls.reason: Eight configured monitors do not prove complete function, region, downstream and failure-path telemetry or correct detection.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Dashboards can include every metric type while an unregistered function or dependency saturation remains invisible.

controls.reason: Four fault tests do not establish complete providers, regions, event states, combinations, timing and continuity oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Single-fault drills can pass while delayed events during partial region failure are lost.

controls.reason: A serverless release policy can define five exact versioning, alias, traffic-shift, rollback and event-compatibility behaviors.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A workflow without rollback or compatibility definition fails the finite policy schema.

controls.reason: Absence of unbounded invocation chains and recursion is a universal runtime and graph claim with dynamic triggers and data-dependent paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Static analysis and capped tests can pass while an indirect cross-service trigger loop grows without bound.

controls.reason: A cost-forecast model can require separate abuse, recursive-loop and large-event amplification scenarios with versioned inputs and calculation outputs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting one scenario or using an unbound calculation input fails the finite forecast manifest; accuracy is not inferred.

controls.reason: Correct classification of eight healthcare data classes requires regulated-domain, privacy and contextual interpretation plus complete data discovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded field can have a label while a derived research value is misclassified or an unknown copy remains unclassified.

controls.reason: Emergency-access protection across all paths plus adequate limits and review requires security, clinical and human judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Logging and approvals can exist while an emergency role is too broad or reviews fail to recognize misuse.

controls.reason: A regulated data schema and append-only history can require preservation of eight exact provenance, unit, range, time, author, status, correction and version fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record or transformation missing units, correction lineage or version fails the finite schema and provenance-chain checks.

controls.reason: A healthcare operations catalog can require four exact human-review, correction, escalation and downtime procedures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting correction or downtime handling fails the finite procedure schema; clinical quality is not inferred.

controls.reason: Five continuity test labels do not provide complete clinical workflows, devices, providers, regions, combinations and safety oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each fault can pass separately while identity and network failure together blocks an essential patient workflow.

controls.reason: Clinical or regulated invariants and complete migration reconciliation require specialist authority, data completeness and substantive correctness oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Counts can reconcile while units change incorrectly or a clinically significant relationship is lost.

controls.reason: A regulated reporting catalog can require four exact incident, breach, safety and regulatory reporting procedures with authority and version bindings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing breach or safety-report procedure fails the finite catalog; legal sufficiency is not inferred.

controls.reason: Transparency of five public-sector processes is a user, administrative-law and accessibility judgment, not a document-presence fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All five procedures can be published while decision reasons remain opaque or appeal is practically unusable.

controls.reason: A public service can be checked for published status, maintenance, accessibility, privacy, security-contact and support resources at stable locations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting any of the six resources or returning an unapproved version fails the finite publication schema.

controls.reason: Four scenario executions do not establish realistic peak, deadline, emergency and coordinated-abuse scale, combinations or public-service outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A nominal civic-event load test can pass while coordinated abuse during a deadline overwhelms identity verification.

controls.reason: Operation during disasters and four correlated failure categories is an availability and continuity claim over undefined severity, duration and dependencies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Documented alternate paths can exist while regional and supplier failure together makes the service unavailable.

controls.reason: Required languages and accessibility depend on population, law, content and assistive technologies; automated tests cannot prove notices and forms are usable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Published translations can be incomplete or misleading and a form can pass machine checks while failing screen-reader users.
